# Risk memo: Tech heavy

_Written by openai/gpt-oss-120b (openai). Verified: 0 unsupported numbers, 39 figures traced to code._

## Summary

The Tech heavy portfolio aims to capture growth in the technology sector while benchmarking against SPY. Over the analysis window from 2016-11-01 to 2026-10-29 it delivered a strong compound annual growth rate of 33.90% with a Sharpe ratio of 1.08.

## Return and risk profile

Annualized volatility of the portfolio was 27.95%, higher than the benchmark's 17.95%. The beta of 1.33 indicates greater sensitivity to market moves. downside risk is reflected in a maximum drawdown of -45.07% occurring between 2021-11-19 and 2022-11-03 and lasting 384 trading days. The Sortino ratio of 1.72 and Calmar ratio of 0.75 show how returns compare to downside volatility and drawdown respectively. The top risk contributor, NVDA, accounts for 29.80% of portfolio volatility despite a weight of 20.00%.

## Tail risk

One‑day 95% historical VaR is 2.93% with an expected shortfall of 4.10%. The 99% historical VaR rises to 4.85% and its expected shortfall to 6.05%. Back‑testing shows the 95% VaR is consistent (122 exceptions versus 113.2 expected). The 99% VaR back‑test verdict is model underestimates risk. Monte‑Carlo simulation suggests a 47.15% chance of a loss over the next year and a 65.89% chance of a drawdown worse than one fifth of value, with a median projected return of 1.89%.

## Stress and regimes

Historical stress testing across four scenarios shows the worst loss in the 2022 rate shock scenario at -40.49%, with the benchmark down -24.50%. Other stress returns were -36.30%, -30.74%, and -27.77%. The current market regime is identified as Calm with a probability of 90.37%. In stress regimes volatility is expected to be 4.5x higher than in calm periods. The best forecast model for next‑month volatility is GARCH-t, which outperformed LightGBM, and the current forecast is 25.42%.

## Disclosed risks from filings

- Business and financial results could be materially affected by macroeconomic downturns, competitive pressures, and supply chain disruptions as described in the risk factors of the holdings. ([META 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm)) ([AAPL 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019325000079/aapl-20250927.htm)) ([AMZN 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000004/amzn-20251231.htm)) ([MSFT 10-K FY2026, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm)) ([NVDA 10-K FY2026, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000021/nvda-20260125.htm))
- Adverse economic conditions may lead to reduced liquidity, credit constraints, and lower demand for products, impacting portfolio performance. ([AAPL 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019325000079/aapl-20250927.htm))

## Caveats and limitations

All figures are based on historical data and model assumptions; actual future performance may differ.

- All figures are historical estimates from daily data between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29; future losses can be larger.
- Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall assume the past is representative of the future; the normal-distribution versions understate fat tails.
- Monte Carlo results depend on the assumed annual return of 5.00% and resample past daily returns.
- Regimes come from a hidden Markov model fitted to the benchmark; the current regime uses only data up to the last date.
- Disclosed risks summarize the latest 10-K risk factors; ETFs and funds have none.
- The prose was written by a language model. Every figure was inserted by code from computed results and checked by an automatic verifier.

_Educational tool, not investment advice. Models are simplifications; historical risk measures can understate future losses._
